## Filtering the FASTQ files for polishing

The first attempts to run ntEdits [@Warren2019] end up with a `std::bad_alloc` error,
which may be due to insufficient memory. The assembly is about 453 million
base pairs (<0.5 Gb), which is much less than the 20 Gb-genomes reported to be
polished with ntHits in less than 30 minutes with 90 Gb of RAM [@Warren2019]
(we have 250 Gb). The main difference between the examples reported in the
original article and our attempt may be the size of the bloom filter (BF). While the
authors used 17$\times$ sequence data for the bloom filter, we have probably more
than double that (~35$\times$, in two FASTQ files).

Too much data in the FASTQ files could be the problem. Below, I use `vsearch` to get
statistics of the expected number of errors per read in the first FASTQ file,
then I filter the file to reduce the size and remove errors before running the
`ntcard` and `nthits` programs.

```{bash eestats2}
FASTQ1=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_1.fastq.gz
FASTQ2=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_2.fastq.gz

if [ ! -e eestats1.txt ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_eestats2 $FASTQ1 \
           --output eestats1.txt \
           --ee_cutoffs 0.5,0.75,0.85,0.95,1
fi

if [ ! -e eestats2.txt ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_eestats2 $FASTQ2 \
           --output eestats2.txt \
           --ee_cutoffs 0.5,0.75,0.85,0.95,1
fi

if [ ! -e eestats_summary.txt ]; then
   gawk 'BEGIN{
      START = 0
      print "Length\tMaxEE0.50\tMaxEE0.75\tMaxEE0.85\tMaxEE0.95\tMaxEE1.00\tFile"
   }(START == 1){
      gsub(/[\(\)]/, "", $0)
      print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $4 "\t" $6 "\t" $8 "\t" $10 "\tFASTQ1"
   }(/----/){START = 1}' eestats1.txt > eestats_summary.txt
   gawk 'BEGIN{
      START = 0
   }(START == 1){
      gsub(/[\(\)]/, "", $0)
      print $1 "\t" $2 "\t" $4 "\t" $6 "\t" $8 "\t" $10 "\tFASTQ2"
   }(/----/){START = 1}' eestats2.txt >> eestats_summary.txt
fi
```

```{r eestatsPlots}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
eestats <- read.table('eestats_summary.txt', header = TRUE)
eestats_L <- pivot_longer(eestats, 2:6, names_to = 'MaxEE', values_to = 'NumReads')
ggplot(data = eestats_L, mapping = aes(x = Length, y = NumReads, color = MaxEE)) +
   geom_line() + facet_wrap(~File)
```

```{bash filter}
FASTQ1=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_1.fastq.gz
FASTQ2=../../data/Shotgun_Illumina/IBC_2_Ex71_6_2.fastq.gz

if [ ! -e filtered1.fasta ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_filter $FASTQ1 \
           --fastaout filtered1.fasta \
           --fastq_maxee 0.5
fi

if [ ! -e filtered2.fasta ]; then
   vsearch --fastq_filter $FASTQ2 \
           --fastaout filtered2.fasta \
           --fastq_maxee 0.5
fi
```

```{bash}
for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e filtered1_k$k.hist ]; then
      ntcard -k $k -t 16 -p filtered1 filtered1.fasta
   fi
done

for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e filtered2_k$k.hist ]; then
      ntcard -k $k -t 16 -p filtered2 filtered2.fasta
   fi
done
```

```{r kmerFreqs}
k31 <- read.table('filtered1_k31.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
k47 <- read.table('filtered1_k47.hist', skip = 2,

plot(k31$multiplicity, k31$frequency, type = 'l',
     xlim = c(0, 50), ylim = c(5.0e+05, 1.0e+09),
     log = 'y', xlab = 'Multiplicity',

lines(k47$multiplicity, k47$frequency, col = 'darkgreen')
lines(k61$multiplicity, k61$frequency, col = 'darkblue')

#abline(v = 5, col = 'darkgreen', lty = 2)
abline(v = 4, col = 'darkblue', lty = 2)


k31 <- read.table('filtered2_k31.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
k47 <- read.table('filtered2_k47.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
k61 <- read.table('filtered2_k61.hist', skip = 2,
                  col.names = c('multiplicity', 'frequency'))
plot(k31$multiplicity, k31$frequency, type = 'l',
     xlim = c(0, 50), ylim = c(5.0e+05, 1.0e+09),
     log = 'y', xlab = 'Multiplicity',
     ylab = 'Frequency', col = 'darkred')
lines(k47$multiplicity, k47$frequency, col = 'darkgreen')
lines(k61$multiplicity, k61$frequency, col = 'darkblue')
abline(v = 6, col = 'darkred', lty = 2)
#abline(v = 5, col = 'darkgreen', lty = 2)
abline(v = 4, col = 'darkblue', lty = 2)
```

The sequenced reads were shortenned from 150 to 140 bp. The reason why longer kmers
have lower coverage peaks is just that any fragment of a chromosome
has a lower chance of being fully contained in a fixed-length, randomly located read,
the longer the fragment is. The high coverage of error-free 31-mers distinguish them
from low-frequency, error-containing 31-mers. Thus, I'd suggest we use $k=31$ for
polishing.

```{bash nthits}
FASTA1=filtered1.fasta
FASTA2=filtered2.fasta

for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e filtered_k$k.bf ]; then
      nthits --threads 16 \
             --kmer $k \
             --pref filtered \
             --outbloom \
             --solid \
             $FASTA1 $FASTA2 1> nthits_k$k.log 2> nthits_k$k.err
   fi
done
```

```{bash ntedit}
ASSEMBLY=../2023-05-12/flye/ONT_PB/assembly.fasta

for k in 31 47 61; do
   if [ ! -e ntedit_k${k}_edited.fa ]; then
      ntedit -t 32 \
             -f $ASSEMBLY \
             -r filtered_k$k.bf \
             -b ntedit_k$k \
             -v 1 1> ntedit_k$k.log 2> ntedit_k$k.err
   fi
   if [ ! -e changes_k$k.tsv ]; then
   # In the original file, not all lines have the same number of columns.
      cut -f 1,2,3,4,5 ntedit_k${k}_changes.tsv > changes_k$k.tsv
   fi
done
```

```{r stats}
changes_k31 <- read.table('changes_k31.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t',
                          col.names = c('contig', 'position',
                                        'original', 'newbase', 'support'))
changes_k47 <- read.table('changes_k47.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t',
                          col.names = c('contig', 'position',
                                        'original', 'newbase', 'support'))
changes_k61 <- read.table('changes_k61.tsv', header = TRUE, sep = '\t',
                         col.names = c('contig', 'position',
                                       'original', 'newbase', 'support'))
changes_k31$change <- paste(changes_k31$original,
                            changes_k31$newbase,
                            sep = ':')
changes_k47$change <- paste(changes_k47$original,
                            changes_k47$newbase,
                            sep = ':')
changes_k61$change <- paste(changes_k61$original,
                            changes_k61$newbase,
                            sep = ':')

profile31 <- as.data.frame(table(changes_k31$change))
profile31$k <- 31
profile31$RelFreq <- profile31$Freq / sum(profile31$Freq)
profile47 <- as.data.frame(table(changes_k47$change))
profile47$k <- 47
profile47$RelFreq <- profile47$Freq / sum(profile47$Freq)
profile61 <- as.data.frame(table(changes_k61$change))
profile61$k <- 61
profile61$RelFreq <- profile61$Freq / sum(profile61$Freq)
z <- rbind(profile31, profile47, profile61)
z2 <- pivot_wider(z, names_from = k, values_from = c('Freq', 'RelFreq'))
z2[is.na(z2)] <- 0
class(z2) <- 'data.frame'
z2$TotFreq <- z2$Freq_31 + z2$Freq_47 + z2$Freq_61
t <- order(z2$TotFreq, decreasing = TRUE)
class(z) <- 'data.frame'
z$Var1 <- ordered(z$Var1, levels = z2[t, 'Var1'])
z$k <- factor(as.character(z$k))
f <- z$RelFreq >= 0.02
ggplot(z[f,], aes(x = k, y = RelFreq, fill = Var1)) + geom_bar(stat = 'identity')
ggplot(z, aes(x = as.numeric(Var1), y = Freq, color = k)) +
   geom_line() + xlim(0, 20)
```
